correctness.rationale: For u the odd part of n with exactly three binary zeros, N=u-1 has h-3 ordinary one-digits. The hyperbinary–halving bijection via eligible cut F_e(t)=1+L_t+R_t-t=0 is reversible and strictly decreasing in t; W>=h-1 and W=h-3 expansions admit cuts, while W=h-2 precisely single splits of beginnings of ordinary one-runs are all inadmissible (including leading-bit split where the only zero cut has a 2 above). Thus s(n)-a(n)=rho(u-1), with four attainable values witnessed by u=17,35,75,171; even-factor invariance extends to every n. Fresh independent integer recurrence compared all 1365 eligible odd u<65536; this finite check supplements the all-length carry proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general algorithm computing each a(n) is broader computational scope but does not imply the new uniform closed-form run-count theorem without the nontrivial one-carry proof.
